Appendix III presents the incidence of suicidal deaths in the States, Union Territories and Cities by three age groups viz : (a) Persons upto 18 years ; (b) Persons between 18 years to 30 years and (c) Above 30 years. It has been observed that, on an average, 43.7% of the persons who committed suicides were in the age group of 18 to 30 years. Almost all the States, Union Territories and Cities conform to all-India pattern in this regard.
Distribution of suicides by sex in the States, U. Ts. and Cities.

Appendix IV furnishes the statistics of suicides by sex. On an average 60.1% of suicides are committed by males. Barring the States of Assam, Jammu and Kashmir and Punjab, all other States generally reflect the all-India pattern. Although the percentage of males committing suicides varies from State to State, one consistent fact is that, in every State and Union Territory, males were more prone to commit suicides than females.
Distribution of suicides by different causes in the States, U.Ts. and Cities.

Appendix V presents the motivating factors which prompted people to commit suicides. It is observed that the largest single cause was despair over dreadful diseases (17.4%). Quarrels with parents-in-law and married partners accounted for 14.4% of the suicides. The pattern of the distribution due to different causes varies from State to State, but the deviation from the all-India pattern is not very significant in most of the States.
Distribution of suicides by the means adopted in the States, U. Ts. and Cities.

Appendix VI exhibits the statistics of suicides by the means adopted for the purpose. It is observed that a large proportion of the persons, who decided on self-destruction, adopted three principal means viz. drowning, hanging and poisoning which account for 23.7%, 19.2% and 20.2% suicides respectively. The pattern is the same in the various States and Union Territories. In important cities, there is deviation from the all-India pattern.
